comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 curriculum; Dutch part-time target, six-year recommended pacing
comparator.sourceNotes: The permanent target remains the Dutch part-time offering, not a separate English or full-time degree. Annex 1 supplies the selected comparative Religie en Levensbeschouwing route: ten 6-EC units in academic stage 1, ten 6-EC positions in stage 2, and 30-EC minor/profiling plus five 6-EC units in stage 3. Academic-stage totals are 60+60+60=180; the part-time table distributes these over six calendar years at 36,24,36,24,36,24 EC. The current route name is not conflated with the differently described Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving programme starting in 2027. Article 10.4 specifies Dutch instruction in the first two academic stages, some English courses, and English instruction in the selected third stage; normalized instruction metadata includes NLD and ENG while raw Dutch provenance is retained. Four restricted positions are instantiated using the first-listed eligible alternative in each period, independently of UCR fit. Alternatives are not stacked. The 30-EC minor remains generic: Article 12.1 allows a qualifying minor or approved academic courses (at least 12 EC level 300), or placement up to 12 EC plus 18 EC courses; applicable approval, entry and non-overlap rules remain. The 0-EC Dutch test is embedded in Geschiedenis van de Wereldfilosofie, not added as credit. Research Lab: Preparation Thesis requires 120 EC, the analytic-methodologies lab follows participation in preparation, and the thesis follows completed preparation. Adopted current rules establish a pathway, not guaranteed future timetable availability. Re-audit 17 October 2026 reopens and confirms the adopted route/credits and part-time table directly. Current marketing redirects to a programme explicitly starting in 2027; it is not substituted for the 2026–2027 route. Article 9.1 additionally requires completion of all first-stage and first-semester second-stage units before preparation; its 120-EC threshold is not the sole condition. Current course-level pages independently checked for world philosophy, myth/ritual and Social Sciences. Social Sciences is substantive religion-focused theory, not a generic methods module; it remains unmatched. Adjudication 2026-10-18 retains this external reconstruction and all prior source work. The previously approved UCR composition is withdrawn on target-comparability grounds and preserved byte-for-byte in the dated review evidence; its mechanical validity is not disputed.

routeSelection.basis: Retain the previously selected comparative, multireligious Religie en Levensbeschouwing route as the least specialized route of the generic target. The adopted 2026–2027 OER controls its reconstruction; future 2027 marketing labels do not rename this route. Restricted alternatives follow official list order without reference to UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: Theology and Religious Studies at VU Amsterdam examines religious traditions, beliefs, texts and practices, and their place in society. The curriculum shown uses the 2026–2027 Religion and Worldviews route, which combines study of several traditions with philosophy, social perspectives and research. The selected offering is part-time.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers individual courses on myth, philosophy and religious art or heritage. These provide useful related perspectives, but the available courses do not sustain a programme centred on religious traditions, sacred texts and lived religion. We therefore show VU’s complete curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

exception.reason: The available UCR courses provide genuine study of myth, philosophical questions and particular religious-cultural examples. The tested 24-course composition is coherent as philosophy and cultural interpretation, but it does not sustain the study of religious traditions, sacred interpretation and lived religion that defines this target. Its general social, legal and literary courses do not establish those religious applications. No defensible target-level UCR comparison is established by the current evidence; this is not a requirement for disciplinary equivalence or a minimum count of matching rows.
exception.curriculumContext: Retained independently verified 180-EC Religie en Levensbeschouwing route, Dutch part-time over six calendar years, with all 26 components, selected restricted choices, research/thesis requirements and 30-EC approved profiling space. No external-curriculum blocker is asserted.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: All 24 selected courses were re-examined in the current 151-row enriched workbook. World Myth & Literature and Western Philosophy have genuine partial correspondences; archaeology, African art, ancient democracy, Buddhist self-theory, Aquinas/natural law and literary representations of religion make further specific contributions even without shared rows. They are acknowledged, not counted as irrelevant. Much of the remaining curriculum supplies general philosophy, criticism, social theory, law and political thought without a required or documented religious object of inquiry. Their course-to-generic-meaning-concept fit does not establish that concept as a response to this religion-centred target. VU article 10.3 requires engagement with religious/worldview traditions and claims, interreligious comparison/dialogue and related disciplinary perspectives. Course pages confirm religion-focused social science, fieldwork in religious communities, sacred-text hermeneutics and philosophies/theologies of religion. No compulsory biblical languages, professional licensing or exact course equivalence is imposed on the general route. All 151 course identities and relevant profile/description content were screened for possible bounded repairs; Youth Resilience to Extremism adds generic radicalisation/resilience research and Native American Histories adds Indigenous cultural inquiry, but neither establishes the missing programme-level religious inquiry. The 30-EC unspecified VU minor and optional UCR research are not populated with invented teaching. A few substitutions or a more cautious label cannot repair this substantive absence. See course-by-course challenge and adjudication report for the strongest argument on each side.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative religious cultures, texts and worldviews
candidateAssessment.assessment: The broader meaning concept has genuine philosophical/myth/material-cultural connections but does not sustain comparison of religious traditions, sacred interpretation and lived religion. Several owned interests are not implemented: general literary reading is not sacred-text hermeneutics, social influence is not religious belief/coping, and general civic institutions are not religious practice.

Actual conflict, radicalisation and environmental courses can supply complementary perspectives; no required religion-centred inquiry or documented religious-environment/dialogue sequence is established. Rejection as merely redundant with the withdrawn public-life strand is superseded.

The specific art/literary/philosophical contributions do not establish theological/biblical interpretation, doctrine or lived-faith formation. Missing professional credentials are not used to reject the general comparative route.

Islamic courts as artistic context and comparative public law do not establish Islamic belief, history, exegesis or jurisprudence. Arabic remains support-only under the retained corrected evidence classification.
